accuracy.evidence: Checked against the Pompeii Archaeological Park (pompeiisites.org), the British Museum 'Life and death in Pompeii and Herculaneum' resources, the Smithsonian Global Volcanism Program entry for Vesuvius and USGS volcano hazards pages: Pompeii lies about 10 km from the crater; the AD 79 eruption was explosive (Plinian), dropping about 2.8 m of pumice and ash on Pompeii over roughly 18 hours, followed next morning by pyroclastic density currents, for 4–6 m of deposits in all; no lava reached the town; people did not recognise Vesuvius as a volcano; organic remains such as the 81 carbonised loaves in the bakery of Modestus and wall paintings survived; Giuseppe Fiorelli began plaster casting of voids in 1863 (the dog cast, House of Vesonius Primus, 1874); excavation began in 1748 (1748 − 79 = 1,669 years); a population of about 11,000 is the commonly cited estimate. The adult text flags that the traditional 24 August date is disputed, so the lesson uses AD 79 only. Parameterised answers (10n, a+b, 2n, d−1) were enumerated by the validator.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the common child ideas reported in KS2 teaching guides from the British Museum and Historical Association: lava buried Pompeii (step 1 predict, challenge tag lava twice, mastery m8, sorter card), the plaster figures are Roman statues or people turned to stone (step 3 predict, tags statue and tostone, p5), things buried for centuries must all rot or all turn to stone (step 2 predict), the town was always known or the eruption and rediscovery dates are confused (timeline task, tag found, m1), and Pompeii is special because it was the only Roman town (tag only, m9). Each wrong answer has its own message.

lab_distinct.evidence: gate_lab_distinct passed. Related volcano labs are 560 What is a volcano (flagvolc: build a cutaway, magma vs lava) and 583 Why earthquakes happen (flagearthq). This lab is about a historical eruption and its archaeology: an hour-by-hour ash-depth model on a town with no lava, preservation by burial, Fiorelli's casting sequence, a dated timeline and reading finds as evidence. None of these mechanics exist in any other lab and they could not be reused for another topic by relabelling.

lab_teaches.evidence: Learners discover before being told: tapping Vesuvius shows ash depth climbing 0 → 1 → 2 → 2.8 → 5 m over the houses with no lava drawn; dropping objects into the ash reveals how each one was kept; the cast step refuses out-of-order moves with the physical reason (dig first and the hollow crumbles); placing timeline cards forces the order AD 79 → hidden → 1748 → today and ends with 1748 − 79 = 1,669; digging and matching finds turns objects into evidence. The banner states each rule only after the task is won.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions with tempting wrong options: 'Rivers of red-hot lava' for what buried Pompeii (the most common belief), 'They all rot away' and 'They all turn into solid stone' for objects buried 1,700 years, and 'Statues the Romans carved' or 'The real people turned to stone' for the figures. The lab then shows ash, preserved objects and plaster filling a hollow, and the task message reports the prediction against the right answer.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions, each wrong option tagged with its own feedback: lava, wave, stone, looked, statue, tostone, book, only, found, recent. For example choosing 'Rivers of red-hot lava' explains pumice and ash fell then hot ash clouds rushed over the town; choosing 1748 explains that is when digging began, not the eruption. Correct answers build a streak.

readability.evidence: Kid text scores Flesch-Kincaid 3.5 (limit 6.5) and adult text 6.1 (limit 9.5). Sentences are short; volcano, erupt, pumice, ash, plaster, hollow and archaeologist are explained in plain words in context. Lab buttons use plain verbs ('Move the clock on', 'Bury in ash: Coins', 'Dig patch 2', 'Add to timeline'). The topic of people who died is handled gently: 'Some people and animals could not escape', and the cast shown is a dog.

no_filler.evidence: gate_content found no filler phrases and the explanation shares under 12% of 6-word shingles with every other lesson. Each kid paragraph carries one part of the story (the town, the eruption, preservation and casts, rediscovery and finds); the adult text gives standards, sources, the task list and common mistakes, including the date caveat.

mobile.evidence: Checked on 360 px screenshots in light and dark themes before and after Show me at every step (/workspace/shots/pom-*, pomd-*). After the first pass the eruption cloud was clipped to the panel (it covered the banner), the hour and depth label got its own white box, and the timeline rows were given short labels ('Buried by Vesuvius', 'Digging begins') because long text overlapped the date column at 360 px. Cards, ash pit, cast steps, timeline slots and clue rows now fit without clipping, and every action has a full-width button.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs passed on desktop and iPhone 13: all five tasks complete with Show me, the challenge shows, axe WCAG 2.1 AA is clean in both themes, and there are no console errors. Every canvas action has a button (Move the clock on, Bury in ash, cast step buttons, Add to timeline, Dig patch n, Pick then 'tells us'), the canvas aria-label is rewritten after each action (hour and ash depth, items in the ash, cast steps done, timeline so far, finds dug and matched), and feedback is announced through c.say.
